name: Halley's comet (1986)
description: Halley's comet on one whole 76-year orbit around the Sun, from 1948 to 2024, centred on its last return, when it rounded the Sun on 9 February 1986. Its orbit is a long, thin ellipse (eccentricity 0.97) that reaches out beyond Neptune, and it goes round the wrong way, against the planets (inclination 162°). It moves fast near the Sun and crawls far out, as Kepler's second law says. Elements at perihelion from JPL.
